original_value: The performance of data-driven learning approaches is often unsatisfactory when the training data is inadequate either in quantity or quality. Manually labeled privileged information (PI), \eg attributes, tags or properties, is usually incorporated to improve classifier learning. However, the process of manually labeling is time-consuming and labor-intensive. To address this issue, we propose to enhance classifier learning by extracting PI from untagged corpora, which can effectively eliminate the dependency on manually labeled data. In detail, we treat each selected PI as a subcategory and learn one classifier for per subcategory independently. The classifiers for all subcategories are then integrated together to form a more powerful category classifier. Particularly, we propose a new instance-level multi-instance learning (MIL) model to simultaneously select a subset of training images from each subcategory and learn the optimal classifiers based on the selected images. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of our approach.

result.paraphrase: Data-driven learning methods often perform poorly when the training set is insufficient in either size or quality. To improve classifier training, manually labeled privileged information (PI), such as attributes, tags, or properties, is typically added, but labeling is both time-consuming and labor-intensive. To overcome this limitation, we propose extracting PI from untagged corpora to enhance classifier learning and remove the dependence on manually annotated data. Specifically, each chosen PI is regarded as a subcategory, and an independent classifier is learned for each subcategory. These subcategory classifiers are then combined into a stronger category classifier. In particular, we introduce a new instance-level multi-instance learning (MIL) model that simultaneously selects a subset of training images from each subcategory and learns the optimal classifiers from the selected images. Extensive experiments show the advantage of our method.
